correctness.rationale: For the defined simple cubic GP(10,2), a block is eligible exactly when it is independent and no outside vertex has two neighbors in it. The least-uncovered-vertex recurrence counts partitions of fixed vertices without ordering the blocks. A separately written exhaustive implementation reproduced the polynomial 1+20t+100t^2+120t^3+90t^4+10t^6, no four-block partition, and 212 five-block partitions with the three profiles 60, 100 and 52. At most three blocks cannot cover 20 vertices (each block has size at most six). Exactly two five-block partitions are square colorings. Independently, fixing the colors on the even inner pentagon as 0,...,4, the even outer vertices at 2a are restricted to a±2 mod 5. The distance-two constraints around this outer five-cycle force a constant choice of sign. The odd outer vertices are then forced by their two adjacent even outer and two distance-two even inner vertices; their colors are a+4 for the plus sign and a+2 for the minus sign at 2a+1. The odd inner colors are then forced to a+1 and a, respectively. Both assignments satisfy the constraints. The modulo-five quotient is locally bijective, so counts of each neighbor color pull back; Petersen has minimum six, independently reproduced. Thus the decrease is strict and 210 of the 212 optimal partitions fail to color the square.
residual_risks: The exact counts are graph-specific; no classification of automorphism orbits or higher-order generalized Petersen graphs is verified.
